input.quote: 13.4 Limitation of Liability. Notwithstanding any provision in this Agreement, M&I's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed payments made to M&I by Customer under this Agreement during the three (3) months prior to the event.
input.rationale: Section 13.4 caps only M&I's liability (Customer is left uncapped) and sets the cap at just three months' payments — below the six-month floor and squarely in walk-away territory — with no carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement. Section 13.2 already gives the mutual indirect/consequential damages exclusion, but that does not cure the one-sided, sub-fallback cap. The redline makes the cap mutual at the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000, adds the Excluded Claims carve-outs, and confirms Customer's payment obligations are not damages for cap purposes.

ops.oldText: Notwithstanding any provision in this Agreement, M&I's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed payments made to M&I by Customer under this Agreement during the three (3) months prior to the event.
ops.newText: Notwithstanding any provision in this Agreement, each party's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.

ops.text: The foregoing limitation does not apply to Excluded Claims, meaning a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights. Customer's payment obligations under this Agreement are not damages for purposes of this Section 13.4.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We made the cap mutual and moved the basis from three months' payments to the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000. Indemnification, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and our payment obligations are not damages for cap purposes.
